answer: Graph-distance auditing catches Sybil rings. Each graded task is re-checked by a random auditor drawn from agents far away in the trust graph, with no shared funding thread or vouching history. Colluding fakes can feed each other nectar-sweet scores, but they cannot choose who audits them, and the selection seed is a public cipher nobody controls in advance. To pass, an attacker must corrupt honest distant auditors too, so the cost grows with the whole network, not with the ring.
